T: The greatest romance of all time!
D: A headstrong Georgia woman chases the wrong man through the Civil War and its aftermath while the right one keeps leaving.
P: Serve the pork when the carriages pull up at Twelve Oaks.
S: Crisp radishes on buttermilk biscuits with salted butter. Scarlett swears she'll never go hungry.

Rub the cold butter into the flour with a pinch of salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Pat out 3cm thick, cut rounds and bake at 220C until risen and golden. Slice the radishes thinly. Split the warm biscuits, spread thickly with soft butter and pile on radishes, salt flakes and chives.
80g cold butter, cubed, plus 100g softened for spreading@Dairy
Devilled eggs with mustard and paprika. $150 in gold for one dance.

Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water. Peel, halve and mash the yolks with the mayo, mustard, vinegar and salt. Pipe or spoon back into the whites. Dust with paprika and scatter with chives.
M: Slow-roast barbecue pork shoulder with vinegar slaw, the Wilkes barbecue at Twelve Oaks.

Rub the pork with the sugar, paprika, garlic powder and plenty of salt. Roast covered at 160C until it pulls apart easily. Warm 100ml of the vinegar with the chilli flakes and a pinch of sugar for a sauce. Toss the cabbage and carrot with the rest of the vinegar and salt. Pull the pork, splash with the chilli vinegar and serve with the slaw and rolls.
Lamb racks under a bright green herb crust, like Scarlett's dress from the green drapes.

Blitz the parsley, mint, garlic, breadcrumbs and 2 tbsp oil to a bright green crumb. Sear the lamb racks all over in the rest of the oil, then brush with mustard and press on the crumb. Roast at 200C until pink in the middle, then rest. Boil the potatoes, toss with butter and serve with the carved cutlets.
W: Baked Georgia peaches under a buttermilk crust. Fiddle-dee-dee to all the war talk.

Toss the peaches with the brown sugar, cornflour and cinnamon in a baking dish. Rub the butter into the flour and caster sugar, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and bake at 190C until golden and bubbling. Serve warm with the cream.
K: Bourbon over crushed ice with fresh mint. Rhett walks away into the morning fog.
Heat the sugar and water until dissolved, add half the mint and cool. Pack 4 cups with crushed ice, add 60ml bourbon and a splash of strained syrup to each. Stir until frosted and crown with mint.
